How to become seriously
well-read in your 20s
Read twenty pages a day. It sounds small, but it's about twenty books a year. In ten years, that's more than most people read in their whole life.
Alternate fiction and non-fiction. A novel teaches you about people, a history book teaches you about the world. You need both to understand life.
Keep a list of books people recommend. When someone you admire mentions a book, write it down. Your reading list becomes a map of great minds.
Read the classics slowly. A few pages of Marcus Aurelius or Tolstoy before bed. Old books lasted for a reason, and they change how you see things.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. It fills the gaps between books and makes everything you read click.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It fills the gaps between books and makes everything you read click.

slides.texte_overlay: Talk about what you read. Share one idea with a friend each week. Explaining a book helps you remember it and starts great conversations.
Carry a book everywhere. Waiting rooms, trains, queues. All those lost minutes add up to hours of reading every single week. Use them.
